newsitem.title: INDIA: Indian industry to recover in 2nd half 96/97-CMIE.
newsitem.headline: Indian industry to recover in 2nd half 96/97-CMIE.

text.p: Indian industry is expected to do better in the second half of 1996/97 (April-March) than in the first, the Centre for Monitoring Indian Economy (CMIE) said.

While there were indications of a slowdown in the industrial sector, there were no signs of a recession, the Bombay-based independent research firm said in a report made available to Reuters on Tuesday.
CMIE said its index showed a slowdown in the growth in industrial production to 4.4 percent in the first six months of 1996/97 from 18 percent in the same period last year.
The CMIE index is based on 62 industries accounting for 60 percent of the total weight in the official index of industrial production (IIP), it said.
However early indications at the beginning of the second half of 1996/97 showed a recovery was underway, CMIE said.

"Production statistics available for the month of October 1996, for industries accounting for 45.6 percent of the total weight in the IIP, indicate a recovery in the growth rate from 0.7 percent in September 1996 to 4.6 percent in October 1996."
Most of the infrastructure industries had performed well in October and November 1996, the report added.
It however cautioned that there were some factors which could contain the recovery.

"We had expected that with an excellent monsoon during 1996, hydel (hydro-electric) power generation would pick up. While the decline in hydel power generation has been arrested, the expected increase in output has not (taken place)," it said.
The report warned that the reservoir levels by end-September did not indicate any major increase in hydel power generation and that it could be lower that the levels anticipated by the government.

In addition, a sharp slowdown in sectors such as cement, steel and automobiles during October and/or November as well as a slump in prices of these commodities and others such as tea could dampen the recovery, it said.
"We had earlier projected industrial production to grow by seven percent during 1996/97. This stands revised to 6.5-7.0 percent," CMIE said.
Industrial production grew by 12.6 percent in 1995/96.
